comparison: Perfect agreement on fluid dynamics validation. Both evaluations find strong support for the circular vortex pattern and velocity measurements matching simulations (C21, C27-C31, C103-C104, C126-C127). OpenEval notes the fixed interface shape simplification while peer reviewers emphasize the compelling agreement between theory and experiment.

Both address RNA stability claims (C48-C49). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of calculation details in main text, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, noting that authors made 'convincing arguments supported by simulations' in the revised submission. This suggests peer reviewers had access to additional materials or revisions.

Strong agreement on DNA accumulation findings (C19, C33-C34, C69, C105, C128-C131). Both find the evidence compelling with good agreement between experiment and simulation. OpenEval notes fluorescence fluctuations as measurement uncertainty, while peer reviewers emphasize the convincing demonstration of accumulation via gas flows.

Strong agreement on isothermal DNA replication demonstration (C22, C54-C67, C138-C143). Both evaluations find this central result well-supported with appropriate controls. OpenEval notes air bubble disruptions and Taq polymerase limitations for prebiotic relevance, while peer reviewers view it as 'compelling evidence' and 'exciting proof-of-concept' for the mechanism.

Agreement on speculative nature of future applications (C73, C75). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are 'reasonable hypotheses for future work but not supported by data.' Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, suggesting these as 'potential future experiments' that remain to be tested.

Partial overlap on prebiotic relevance claims (C72, C74, C78, C125). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the extrapolation to prebiotic conditions is speculative given use of Taq polymerase. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, viewing the work as advancing understanding of geological settings for origin of life, though acknowledging further validation needed.

Strong agreement on FRET evidence for spatial separation (C38-C42, C132-C133). Both evaluations find the experimental demonstration of strand annealing/separation zones convincing. OpenEval notes FRET provides indirect rather than direct salt measurement, while peer reviewers emphasize the clear demonstration of hybridization and dissociation in different zones.

Both address salt/DNA oscillations and strand separation capability (C43-C44, C50, C70, C135-C136). OpenEval finds simulation data supporting oscillations but notes lack of direct experimental measurement. Peer reviewers validate the FRET demonstration of the mechanism, focusing on experimental evidence rather than simulation predictions.

Minimal overlap on convection mechanism (C103-C104, C23, C124). OpenEval addresses the core mechanism with experimental observations and mechanistic reasoning. Peer R1 focuses on fluid dynamics validation. Both support the circular flow pattern but address different aspects of the same physical phenomenon.

OpenEval evaluates analogies to Rayleigh-Bénard convection and chaotic variations (C45-C47) as SUPPORTED conceptual framework. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific comparative/analogical arguments.

OpenEval evaluates methodological choices for Taq polymerase use and detection methods (C52-C53, C57) as SUPPORTED and well-justified. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these methodological justifications.

OpenEval evaluates detailed experimental methodology (C24-C26, C79-C102, C122) as SUPPORTED with clear documentation. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these methodological details, though peer reviewers generally affirm experimental rigor.

OpenEval evaluates background literature and context (C1-C18) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these contextual claims, as they focus on novel findings rather than literature review.

OpenEval evaluates simulation methodology and parameters (C32, C112, C119-C121) as SUPPORTED but notes simplifications. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses simulation methodology details, though peer reviewers affirm theory-experiment agreement.

OpenEval rates claim about relative abundance of isothermal vs. thermal gradient environments on early Earth (C77) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of geological evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific geological claim.

Peer reviewers acknowledge air bubble artifacts (C61, C144) as documented limitations that prevent full simulation-experiment correspondence, viewing this as accepted phenomenon rather than critique. OpenEval mentions these disruptions within R5 context but doesn't evaluate as separate result.
